includes: config.get, config.schema, config.schema.lookup, config.set, config.patch, config.apply, config.openFile: the config area's Gateway methods, one entry point each

CLI commands, one entry point each: openclaw config (no subcommand, the guided wizard), openclaw config get, set, patch, unset, file, schema, validate, and openclaw configure; flags, --section values and set modes are not entry points
chat commands, one entry point each: /config show (alias /config get), /config set, /config unset

agent tool actions, one entry point each (kind agent call): the gateway tool's config.get and config.schema.lookup actions; the theme tool's list, get, set and import actions; the system agent openclaw tool's config_get, config_schema, validate_config, config_set, config_set_ref, config_unset and configure_gateway actions

code from other areas, found by the search below: one entry point per file, kind from <area>, always placed in an operation and never excluded as owned by that area; grep src/, ui/src/ and extensions/ outside this area's paths, skip test files (names containing .test., .suite., test-support, test-utils, test-helpers, test-harness, test-shared or test-mocks, test-only modules imported only by tests, and anything under qa-lab), and count a file only when it calls a listed symbol or sends a listed method name; a type declaration, a re-export, an interface member or a stub that only defines a function of the same name is not a call, and neither is a file that names a config method only in a list of names, a permission or scope check, or an audit label without sending it

startup, one entry point each (kind from gateway startup or from CLI): the Gateway startup config load and validation (src/gateway/server-startup-config.ts), the startup migration of legacy keys, the CLI config guard before every command (src/cli/program/config-guard.ts) and its interactive offer to run Doctor
hand editing, one entry point each (kind file edit): a direct edit of openclaw.json picked up by the file watcher, and a direct edit of an $include file picked up by the file watcher

redaction sinks, one entry point each (kind from <area>), exactly those the Redaction section of docs/gateway/logging.md names: console output, file log records, OTLP log records, session transcript text, harness tool-result text before model context, Control UI tool-call events, sessions_history output, diagnostics exports, provider errors, exec approval display, Gateway WebSocket logs

Control UI: every named control rendered by a file under this area's paths is one entry point (kind UI action), whatever setting it writes, including the chat, sidebar, microphone, camera and link preferences shown in Settings; a control rendered in two sections (an account default and its per-device override) counts once in each section; the Settings sidebar links to this area's own pages are one entry point each; a control shown only inside the native apps is excluded as outside a browser harness, one entry each; each route path a router file under the paths registers for this area's pages is one entry point, with its aliases and redirects part of that entry; the moved-section redirects for pre-restructure links and the ?section= deep link are one entry point each; the Settings sidebar links to pages of other areas are shell, listed once as one excluded entry, and the shell controls shared by every page are listed once as another
Gateway methods of other areas that a non-test file under this area's paths names as a string literal: one excluded entry each, consumed from <area>; enumerate with git grep

reading the config file at startup and on every command: JSON5 parsing, $include resolution, ${VAR} substitution, secret refs as written in config, strict validation and the refusal to start on invalid config

saving: atomic replacement, the write lock, baseHash and revision conflicts, clobber guards and the <path>.rejected.<timestamp> save, the .bak ring and last-known-good copy, read-only and Nix-managed config refusing writes
recovery of failed saves and invalid config: openclaw doctor's config repairs reach this area through the files the code-from-other-areas rule finds, kind from update
hot reload: the file watcher, reload modes, reload planning, hot-applied versus restart-required changes, deferred reload under active work, and an invalid reload keeping the last accepted config
schema and migration of config keys: openclaw config schema, config.schema and config.schema.lookup, uiHints tiers, and the legacy key transforms in src/config/legacy*.ts and *-migration.ts
redaction: the redacted config snapshot every reader receives and logging.redactPatterns with the log and transcript redaction it controls

Control UI settings pages: the generic settings form, raw editor, search, save and recovery controls, appearance, language, tab icon, opening links, chat and sidebar preferences, notifications, security, setup and the settings sidebar

document sections that are this area's (walk every heading of every listed document; a heading not named here for a document with a list is recorded as none, owned by the area named in excludes): docs/gateway/configuration.md, docs/gateway/configuration/config-rpc.md, docs/gateway/configuration/hot-reload.md, docs/gateway/configuration/environment-variables.md and docs/cli/config.md: every section; docs/gateway/configuration/common-tasks.md: only "Split config into multiple files ($include)"; docs/gateway/configuration-reference.md: the introduction, "Pages in this reference set" and "Config includes ($include)"; docs/cli/configure.md: the introduction and "Options"; docs/help/faq/config-basics.md: only "What format is the config? Where is it?", "Do I have to restart after changing config?" and "config.apply wiped my config. How do I recover and avoid this?"; docs/gateway/troubleshooting/config-validation-and-probes.md: only "Gateway rejected invalid config" and its subsections; docs/gateway/config-observability.md: only "Logging"; docs/gateway/logging.md: only "Redaction"; docs/gateway/doctor/config-migrations.md: the introduction, "Runtime config migration", "Command-owner target kinds", "Retention policy", "Retired state and config formats", "Cron ownership before roster migration", "Channel account routing during an update", "Channel ownership during an update", "Sender tool policies", "Agent roster migration", "Channel private-network opt-ins", "Channel webhook listeners", "Talk realtime inheritance", "Missing plugins during migration", "Retired TaskFlow Webhooks plugin", "Replay a July 2026 config upgrade" and "Checks 0-2" with its numbered checks; docs/web/control-ui/settings.md: the introduction, "Browser tab icon", "Gateway host status" (its connection modes only), "Language support", "Appearance themes", "Opening links" and "Settings" without its subsections "Side panel keyboard shortcuts" and "This device (macOS and iOS apps)"
excludes: not entry points, and not listed: readers of the runtime config snapshot (loadConfig, getRuntimeConfig, readConfigFileSnapshot and their kin) and other callers of the redaction helpers, which are library use; scripts/**; test files; controls, commands and pages of other areas that a listed document merely mentions; other areas' Control UI pages that save their settings through the shared config capability without naming a config method
apps/** (macOS, iOS, Android, Linux and OpenClawKit callers of config methods): one excluded entry, native app config calls, outside a browser harness
config.changed: one excluded entry, internal broadcast event

src/config/sessions/**, session config files and pages listed in the sessions area (including ui/src/pages/config/session-storage.ts, session-observer-settings.ts, session-sources.ts): owned by sessions; the Session sources switches are one excluded entry

update.run (including the gateway tool's update.run action), update.status, openclaw update and the Updates settings page (ui/src/pages/config/updates*.ts): owned by update, one excluded entry each for update.run, the gateway tool's update.run action, update.status and openclaw update
plugins.* methods, openclaw plugins, Manage plugins and Custom plugin UI sections: owned by plugins, not listed except through the code-from-other-areas rule

channels.* methods, openclaw channels and per-channel settings pages: owned by channels, not listed except through the code-from-other-areas rule; a channel field edited through config.patch is this area's patch operation
openclaw secrets, secrets.* methods, secrets.reload and docs/gateway/config-secrets-env.md: owned by secrets; writing a secret ref with config set is this area's
openclaw backup (whole-state backup and restore): owned by backup, not listed
openclaw gateway call: owned by the gateway CLI, one excluded entry; the config methods it can call are placed
/debug show, set, unset and reset: runtime-only overrides owned by chat commands, one excluded entry

the system agent openclaw tool's configure_search, configure_skills, configure_model_provider, connect_channel and set_default_model actions: owned by web search, skills, models, channels and models, one excluded entry each

memory, MCP, talk, meetings, activity and import-assistant-memory settings pages (ui/src/pages/config/memory*.ts, mcp*.ts, talk*.ts, meeting-capture.ts): owned by memory, mcp, talk and meetings, not listed
models.* methods, Connect provider and Model Setup: owned by models, not listed; model defaults saved through the settings form are this area's form operation
This device (macOS and iOS app settings, /settings/device and /settings/device/permissions): owned by the native apps; outside a browser harness, not listed

agents.* methods, the Settings agent selector, the agent files editor, the native conversation surface and the side panel shortcuts described in the settings document: owned by agents and chat, not listed; the native embed's Back and title header is one excluded entry, shown only inside the native apps

document sections not named in the includes: docs/gateway/configuration/common-tasks.md other tasks and docs/gateway/configuration-reference.md field sections (owned by the areas whose keys they describe); docs/cli/configure.md Gateway, Model and Web sections and Other notes (owned by gateway, models, web search and daemon); the other questions of docs/help/faq/config-basics.md (owned by gateway auth, web search, nodes and browser); "Gateway check warnings" (owned by the gateway CLI); docs/gateway/config-observability.md Audit, Diagnostics and Telemetry; docs/gateway/logging.md sections other than Redaction (owned by logging); the docs/gateway/doctor/config-migrations.md state sections (Deferred compaction checkpoints, Workspace setup, Session settings, Legacy cron delivery settings, Exec approval policy, Claw provenance schema, ACP session metadata, ACP agents' model precedence, Schema publication during a 2026.9.2 update, Native Codex recovery after Tasks removal, Auth credential fields; owned by update); the other docs/web/control-ui/settings.md sections (owned by the areas named above, Environment identity, the sidebar invitation card section and Personal identity by the Control UI shell and profiles)
